html:
Harpylen (F98)

Region in the English scoring table: Bulwar.

In one sentence: Harpylen is a global campaign to give scattered Harpy flocks a common homeland: unify the Harpy Hills through a predecessor, establish the fourth and final Queendom, and extend the Queen’s wings across Halann through roosts, subjects, song magic, and migration routes.

Story: very high | Mission-tree length: long (38 direct missions, excluding predecessor trees) | Mission-tree update: current files updated through 2026-09-07 | Uniqueness: extreme | Tedium: medium-high | Early pressure: predecessor-dependent | Expansion: extreme

Identity and history

Harpylen is not a 1444 starting country. A qualifying Firanyan- or Siadunan-culture Harpy country can form it after the country controls five core roosts in the Harpy Hills and either it or a non-sovereign subject controls at least 100 provinces in Bulwar. Siádan (F48) is excluded. Mulén (F50) is a special exception: it can receive the Harpylen name and Queendom government while retaining its F50 tag and its own mission tree. Ordinary formers switch to F98 and receive the independent Harpylen mission tree.【Local script】

Ayarallen (F27) is the smoothest and most story-appropriate predecessor. Nanšalen (F80) and Hytiranyalen (F81) also provide complete preceding campaigns. The predecessor determines how the unification threshold is reached: Ayarallen excels at matriarchal government and subject politics, Nanšalen leans toward religion and diplomacy, while Hytiranyalen is defined by scholarship and artificery. These missions do not remain alongside the Harpylen tree after formation, so the desired predecessor content should be completed first.【Local script】【Community view】

The name Harpylen predates 1444. The earliest Queendom is tied to the legendary ancestor Firanya; after the first Queendom collapsed in 817 BA, the flocks divided into matriarchal polities. After the Day of Ashen Skies, the Šumiryalen flock established the second Queendom, which lasted until it was destroyed in 487 by the bronze dragon Aakhet. Hytiranyalen and Lisinyalen then formed the third Queendom, which ultimately fell to Amarien’s conquest. Thus the Harpy Hills of 1444 were not a memoryless wasteland, but a collection of rival heirs who remembered the old thrones. These are histories of earlier Queendoms: 817 BA and 487 are not dates for the formation of the current F98 tag.【Wiki material】

National story and campaign arc

Formation is only the prologue. The new Queen must turn “the fourth and final Queendom” from a title into an institution: recognise the internal legal autonomy of the matriarchies, bring matriarchs into a council-like advisory group, and make every roost answer to the throne. The missions develop roosts, public infrastructure, military sites, and trade centres so the mountain homeland can support a wider empire.【Local missions】【Local flavour text】

The story then shifts from unifying Bulwar to finding sisters scattered across the world. After the Queendoms collapsed, Harpies migrated into Cannor, Sarhal, Haless, and Aelantir. Harpylen uses song magic to follow those migration routes, establishes distant roosts, supports local Harpy countries, and incorporates them into a subject system. Centaurs in the Forbidden Plains can be organised into special subjects, and residents of the Deepwoods may form another special subject. The goal is not an ordinary world conquest, but a vast subject network reconnecting every Harpy flock; the territorial requirements nevertheless approach a half-world conquest.【Local missions】【Official development context】

The endgame turns toward Asmalil. Harpylen combines resources from across the world, precursor relics, and elemental artificery to build dedicated magical projects, gradually strengthening Harpy song magic. When the Queen can hear the “song” of every people in the world, the country has transformed from a lost kingdom into a global commonwealth. The ordinary route remains F98 and does not establish a second player formation tag.【Local missions】【Local events】

Core mechanics

Queendom power. The dedicated government mechanic continuously accumulates power, which can support the matriarchies, issue matriarchal edicts, or invoke the Queen’s domination. It can reduce subject liberty desire and aggressive expansion, strengthen subjects, and extract development from subject provinces into the homeland. This is the engine of the subject empire, not a side benefit.【Local government mechanic】

Roost construction. Mountain roosts are more than ordinary provinces. Missions expand roost tiers and add barracks, forts, temples, and markets, with different buildings providing long-term bonuses to all roosts. Expansion and development therefore reinforce one another: conquering a new highland also creates the next airborne city.【Local missions】

Migration and special subjects. The missions track distant Harpy flocks and cultivate different partners in the Forbidden Plains, Deepwoods, Sarhal, and Haless. Harpylen plays as a global network of matriarchies and protected subjects rather than turning every province into the same direct-administration bloc.【Local missions】【Local events】

Song magic and Asmalil. Dedicated projects feed metal, precursor relics, and knowledge from across the world into a research system, strengthening Harpy magic in legitimacy, development, diplomacy, and administration. This is a continuing mid- and late-game magical growth line, not a one-off reward.【Local missions】【Local localisation】

Staged play

Predecessor stage: complete a Harpy starting country’s core story, then secure five key roosts and the 100-province Bulwar threshold. Ayarallen is the smoothest thematic route; Hytiranyalen is harder early but foregrounds scholarship and artificery.

Queendom stage: after forming F98, establish a stable matriarchal subject network, raise Queendom power, and develop mountain roosts. Expanding without managing subjects undermines the central loop.

Global stage: advance along migration routes, secure distant footholds, and complete magical projects. Harpylen supports high aggressive expansion and a large subject empire, while distance, religious-cultural variation, and naval logistics create the real pressure.

Formable country and endgame.

Harpylen is the formable country and remains F98 on the ordinary route. The end state is a connected Harpy commonwealth built through roosts, autonomous matriarchies, special subjects, migration routes, and Asmalil projects. The current source set does not establish a separate successor player tag.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion/building 98/100 | Autocracy/liberty 80/100 | Magic/artifice balance 60/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; thematic intensity 96/100) | Pluralism/uniformity 80/100.

The v2.1 value result is Good (84/100) with a stable trajectory. Opposition to enslavement and clipping, a homeland for scattered Harpies, public infrastructure, and retention of non-Harpy traditions support the positive reading; forced subjectage and subject-development extraction mainly reduce restraint.

Harpylen suits players who enjoy long formation chains, subject networks, global collection, mountain construction, magic projects, and a strong national epic. Avoid it if you dislike large-scale conquest, intercontinental logistics, complex subjects, or losing the predecessor tree on formation.

Community experience

【Community view】A 5/2026 play report describes Queendom power, loyal subjects, magic, and development extraction as a strong snowball; its comments warn that extracting too much subject development can block later provincial-development requirements.

【Community view】A July 2026 campaign report praises the Ayarallen-to-Harpylen transition, story, and special spells, while describing the main tree as close to a half-world conquest. These are player experiences, not proof of mission rules.

Evidence boundary

This article concerns local Mod and translation version v1.37.5.0, retaining the source article’s verification date of 2026-09-23. F98 identity, formation conditions, 38 direct missions, the F50 exception, Queendom power, roosts, special subjects, and magical projects were checked against current local files.

The offline Wiki snapshot is available, but the Harpylen page (page_id=1749, revision_id=25531) redirects to the older Ayarallen identity. This article uses Harpy Matriarchy (4148/22617) only for earlier queendoms and autonomous matriarchy history. It does not let those pages override current F98 scripts. Full source details and version conflicts remain in the evidence page, with the Harpy page recorded as 397/32594.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces current local national-idea texts and script effects. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; seven ideas unlock in order through idea-group investment, and the ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed, without adding racial, government or mission bonuses. Successor ideas do not automatically stack with the old set. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals; they do not establish that those events had already happened in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s native English localisation.

Harpylen — Harpyleni Ideas

Traditions: Harpyleni Traditions

Effect: Infantry combat ability: +15%; morale damage received: -10%.

Idea 1: Birth of a New Queendom

Harpylen; a title given only to the land ruled by a true Queen of all Harpies. First realized by Firanya herself, this title is the dream of all who call themselves Firanya’s children. Many have claimed the title, although few have had any degree of legitimacy. The second Queendom was established by the flock Šumiryalen, and was only felled by the bronze dragon Aakhet himself. The third - an alliance between the Hytiranyalen and Lysinyalen flocks - firmly halted Akalšesi expansion into our hills. This third and most recent queendom fell beneath the Phoenix Legions of Jaher and his general Amarien. Ours is the fourth, and there will be no fifth.

Effect: Liberty desire from subject development: -0.25.

Idea 2: Harpy Diplomacy

Since time immemorial, harpies and their queendoms have been known for complex and conflict-averse foreign policy. The tributary arrangement extracted by Ayarallen from the remnants of Dartaxâgerdim in 1449 persisted more or less unchanged for centuries, despite continual instability across Bulwar, while the fourth Harpylen, which emerged as a nominal ally of the Jadd Empire before accepting the Divine Herald as the recognised overlord of Bulwar, retained extraordinary autonomy compared to other vassal polities of the period. Harpylen’s position at a crossroad of the Serpentspine, the Deepwoods, the Forbidden Plains and Bulwar made careful management of border tensions vital, but beyond this, the matriarchs of Harpylen fostered an institutional gravitas. By the end of the eighteenth century, the figure of the Harpylen diplomat was familiar enough to appear in novels from Anbenncóst to Feiten - they were stately, immensely well-informed, playing a complex and unclear game, and by the denouement very often vindicated.

Effect: Aggressive expansion impact: -20%.

Idea 3: The Odd Hunt

The rivalry between Hytiranyalen and Ayarallen, sometimes fabled to stretch back to the daughters of Firanya herself, was contorted into a different shape as Ayarallen took the helm of a fourth Harpylen. Even Ayarallen could no longer deny the position and prominence of this ancient flock, famed above all for their "Odd Hunt", a practice dating back to the period of harpy history typified by seasonal raiding. A harpy on the Odd Hunt sought out any and all knowledge or information they could find; sourcing rare books, ferreting out technological blueprints or even kidnapping intellectuals for installation in their roosts. Under the fourth Harpylen, this practice took its recognisable modern form, a highly organised system of student exchanges and residencies predominantly conducted with the Overclan and the Jadd Empire. The Harpylen government benefited greatly from this exchange, most notably through the spread and popularisation of artificery from Drolakand and Aqatbar.

Effect: Technology cost: -7.5%.

Idea 4: Queen of Harpykind

All harpies kneel to the Queen of Harpylen, this much is fact. Even those from far distant flocks recognize the position of the Queen, her title holds so much gravitas. The centralization of Harpylen was spearheaded by Ištara II Ayarato, promising autonomy and privileges to the other flocks in return for their support for various local administrative and institutional reforms within their lands. Of course, these concessions could be revoked if needed, and often were when the death of Matriarchs triggered the traditional instant dissolution of local government institutions, causing massive chaos for day to day administration. Tax exemptions and semi-autonomous trade allowances, as well as awarding prestigious, yet reasonable positions in the state hierarchy of Harpylen, were enough to convince most to allow the Ayarato administrators access to their lands and regional governments. With this, Harpylen evolved from a figure-driven empire of Harpies that would disintegrate at the first sign of challenge or death of a major Queen, to a modern state able to withstand and evolve with an ever-changing political and economic landscape.

Effect: Monarch administrative power: +1; Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 5: Trade with the Plain and the Forest

Our hills lie at a crossroads of many important trade routes in and out of the Centaur Plains. We are the final stop between the Plains and both Southern Cannor and the Fey Woods, and we are able to exploit our position along these routes with extreme efficiency. Some of these trade routes are truly ancient, and our connection with the peoples of these lands has been tied into our existence since time immemorial. Our lands are filled with the coin of all corners of the world, and a great many riches have flown through our roosts and markets.

Effect: Global trade power: +10%; Number of merchants: +1.

Idea 6: The Queen's Peace

While the Harpylen state adopted the Jadd as its official religion upon its recognition of the sovereignty of the Divine-Herald over Bulwar, those within the Queendom maintained unparalleled and unprecedented freedoms in both cultural and religious practices. From the harpies of Lake Firanya, holdout followers of The Hunt and it’s practices, to Hytiranyalen, who practiced a kaleidoscope of different faiths as diverse as the books within their libraries, to the humans of Gelkalis and Garlas-Kel, followers of the New and Old Cults respectively, there was no real top-down enforcement of faith within the lands of the Queen. Harpyleni roosts were a metropolis of peoples: followers of Irdaeos from the plains, Fey cultists from the woods, elves and Half-elves from all corners of Cannor and Bulwar. By the eighteenth century, the roosts of Harpylen were extraordinarily religiously diverse and a popular haven for religious minorities fleeing persecution elsewhere - most notably Sun Cultists, Cannorian Pantheists and even elves still following the Forebears.

Effect: Heathen tolerance: +2; Heretic tolerance: +2.

Idea 7: Riches of the Hills

While Harpylen undoubtedly profited from the rich trade between the Plains and their trade partners in Cannor and the Fey Woods, the Harpy Hills were not without riches to call their own, boasting vast mineral wealth. While Harpylen remained poor in lumber and in fields with which to practice agriculture, it was able to tap enormous veins of metal which either remained or became vital to artificery and industrial development. Iron, Copper, Tin, Zinc, Aluminium and more all flowed from innumerable mines dotting the countryside. In comparison with the older Matriarchies, which were disconnected and thus unable to truly exploit the Hills’ mineral wealth, the fourth Harpylen had no such issue. Rich reserves, combined with robust Harpy infrastructure and transport, formed the backbone of the Harpyleni economy in the 17th and 18th centuries, allowing Harpylen to import grain and lumber in enormous quantities from the Overclan and the Jadd Empire.

Effect: Production efficiency: +15%.

Ambition: Harpyleni Ambitions

Effect: Diplomatic annexation cost: -20%.

Ayarallen — Ayaralleni Ideas

Traditions: Ayaralleni Traditions

Effect: Diplomatic relations: +1; Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 1: Legacy of the First Queendom

The first harpy state to appear in Bulwar was established all the way back in 1159 BA by the first Harpy Queen, Firanya. It quickly became one of the dominant forces in Bulwar, controlling much of Northern Bulwar and establishing tributaries on many human city-states in the south. However, with the death of the first Harpy Queen Firanya, her bickering daughters established their own flocks, splitting the once unified Queendom into petty squabbling.

Since then, many have tried to reestablish the once great realm but it was the flock of Ayara that has unified us for the final time against the now weakened Kingdom of Birzartanšes. Only as we unified under the true heir of Firanya could the flocks work together and establish dominance over the Harpy Hills once again.

Effect: Subject force limit contribution: +100%.

Idea 2: Council of Matriarchs

Due to the fractured nature of the flocks, separate cultures arose among the harpies who tried to claim the Queendom. As Mišqa reunited the flocks in 1342, she invited the Matriarchs to become advisors, diplomats and generals in her new order to both appease her new subjects and to use each flock’s strength to their best advantage.

With this, the Council of Matriarchs was established, a congregation of the wisest and strongest harpies who would be entrusted in the administration of the newly reclaimed lands.

Effect: National unrest: -2.

Idea 3: Ištara Swoop

The Ištara Swoop is a special technique used by the Ayaralleni to utilise the cliffs and valleys of the Harpy Hills to descend on their enemies below, shattering formations and crushing morale. It was first utilised by Ayarallen during their clash with the state of Varamhar, where they issued a false retreat into a nearby valley to lure the pursuing eager soldiers into a narrow point.

Once the human army was at the end of the valley, harpy reinforcements appeared from atop the ledges of the canyon and swooped down with talons at the front, slaughtering many of the soldiers there. This one-sided battle deterred many future conquerors from travelling through the Harpy Hills unprepared, as one never knows when they'll be attacked from all fronts.

Effect: Army leader shock: +1.

Idea 4: Tolerant Rulers

While first seen as saviours to the Bulwari people, living under sun elf rule proved to be unlike the freedom the Bulwari people yearned for, and multiple restrictions were set in place from the people first seen as heroes. The Harpy method of governance, meanwhile, was a very loose concept and hardly impacted the Bulwari. Harpies did not impose significant taxes nor did they install governors.

Instead they preferred taking some of the men for mates and leaving those exchange villages as functionally independent with their own elected leaders, businesses and customs. These villages were free to continue practising their religion of choice.

Effect: Liberty desire: +2000%.

Idea 5: Elegant Emissaries

Long have harpies been stigmatised and reduced to being seen as barbaric man-snatchers by both elves and humans. While there may have been a grain of truth in this, we cannot tolerate this reputation any longer. We shall strive to correct our previous grievances and present our new Queendom in a new light.

Harpy emissaries trained in the arts of negotiation and clothed in the finest silks shall be sent to dazzle the various courts with the presence of the most charming diplomats. In time, our emissaries shall reach every corner of the world and bring the greater the respect our Queendom deserves.

Effect: Number of diplomats: +1; Improve relations: +10%.

Idea 6: Plumed Weavings

Inspired by the Gelkar weavers, many harpies have developed a unique form of art called feather tapestries. Skilled artisans meticulously weave together vibrant and colourful feathers of both rare birds from northern Bulwar and harpies to create intricate tapestries that depict mythological stories, historical events, and scenes from everyday life. Often used to educate young harpies and impress foreign dignitaries, they offered a tactile experience of Firanya’s legacy.

These feather tapestries would eventually become a cultural pillar of Harpylen and serve as a way to preserve the cultural heritage of each flock individually, depicting their unique cultures they had developed along with the mixes of elven and human ideas as they further got integrated in Harpyleni society.

Effect: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Idea 7: Skyward Constructions

Our traditional roosts on the highest peaks of the Harpy Hills have long been the centres of our flock’s populations, where the old have settled and where the young took their first flights. Now, as our queendom expands and riches grow, new roosts may join the old.

Each one with grander constructions built by both our harpies and their mates. Atop every mountain harbours the potential for its own settlement, with grand markets and dwellings reaching towards the sky as our great civilisation grows to new heights.

Effect: Construction cost: -10%.

Ambition: Ayaralleni Ambition

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100%.

Nanšalen — Nanšaleni Ideas

Traditions: Nanšaleni Traditions

Effect: Legitimacy: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Devotion: +1; Horde unity: +1; Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 1: Nanša the Farseer

According to the songs, the first matriarch of Nanšalen was Nanša the Farseer, the daughter of Firanya and Gelum-širharu, a powerful mage and ruler of the Pešakizzu; the ancestors of the Gelkar. She had light bluish gray feathers, black hair and red irises, characteristics shared by most Nanšaleni harpies, and she had inherited a great power from her mother and was trained in the arts of farseeing and soothsaying by her father. By the time she reached adulthood, she had surpassed both, and it is said that she could see everything that happened in the Hills; in the past, the present as well as in the future.

To this day, the gift and art of farseeing is common between the Nanšaleni Harpies; even between those who lack magical abilities.

Effect: Mage loyalty equilibrium: +10%.

Idea 2: Gate of Bulwar

After Firanya’s death, Nanša took control of the eastern hills, including the important Invader’s Pass which links Bulwar with the Forbidden Plains.

For millennia, the Nanšaleni controlled who entered Bulwar, inviting the nomadic peoples of the Forbidden Plains, human and centaur alike, to invade the Suran several times throughout history, causing the rise and fall of kingdoms at their whim. But war was not the only thing that went through the gates of Bulwar: a trade route that linked Bulwar with the Lake Federation was established after king Araš VIII and matriarch Ninšara’s expedition to the Serpent’s Gift in 552 AA. While the route declined centuries later, the centaurs of the Serpent’s Gift kept trading with Nanšalen, providing magical materials from the beasts of the plains and šilphalim, a herb popular in Bulwar utilized both in alchemy and as an aphrodisiac.

The control over the gate made the matriarchs of Nanšalen ludicrously wealthy and influential between the flocks of the hills and helped them withstand the sands of time.

Effect: Global trade power: +10%.

Idea 3: The Mahdari

The Mahdari are the royal guard of the matriarch, an elite group of warriors that march to battle as if they were parading, dressed with blue and gold tunics below the scale armor and adorning helmets covered in silver feathers.

Their weapon of choice are the bow and arrow, and they are known as some of the best archers in all of Bulwar. Contrary to other harpies, they prefer to shoot from the ground, where they can better utilize their long composed bows made with Tlalusk’s horns, one of the few materials that allow a harpy to use their full strength with a bow, which gives them more range and accuracy.

The name Mahdari is Bulwari for Immortal, since it is believed that none of the Mahdari ever died on battle, although the real origin of the word is unclear. As the royal guards of the matriarch, they participated in many battles in the Suran plain, the Serpent’s Gift and even Kheterata and the gnoll lands south of the Salahad during Araš VIII’ expeditions.

Effect: Infantry shock: +15%.

Idea 4: Royal Harpies

The Nanšaleni harpies are nicknamed "Royal Harpies" by the Bulwari due to their ties to Akalšes, since the matriarchs of Nanšalen also descend from Araš the First King and the two families are considered one. Ever since the Bulwari Renaissance, when the kings of Akalšes ruled over the plain and the matriarchs of Nanšalen ruled over the hills, it has been customary for every new matriarch to be crowned by the king of Akalšes and, in return, every new king is crowned by the matriarch of Nanšalen.

The matriarchs of Nanšalen wear a crown similar to the Akalšesi one, made of cobalt and silver, and decorated with sapphires from Gemisle. A work of Dwarven craftsmanship, it was commissioned by king Araš VIII to the artisans of Verkal Gulan as a crowning gift for his half-sister, Matriarch Ninšara.

Effect: Prestige: +1.

Idea 5: The Sky-Blue Palace

Wealthy due to the trade with the plains, matriarch Ninšara used her treasures to build a new capital for her flock. Built on the source of the Hatatun river, with easy access to both the Suran plain and the Invader’s Pass, Vainviria became Nanšalen’s majestic roost.

The city is built on several terraces, with the Hatatun falls splitting the city in two. The lower levels are home to bazaars, warehouses and the residences of the human and dwarven inhabitants, while the middle ones, only accessible by flying or via the four massive lifts built by the engineers of Hehodovar, contain the residences of the harpies. The upper level, on the other hand, is dominated by gardens and is home to the palace that gives the roost its name, the Sky-Blue Palace, the residence of the Matriarchs of Nanšalen.

Effect: Construction cost: -10%.

Idea 6: Divine Duty of Queens

Centuries ago, the matriarchs of Nanšalen converted to the Sun Cult due to their relation with Akalšes and adopted the version of the Cult practiced there: the Cult of Kings. This sect of the cult believed that the King of Akalšes was Chosen by Surael to unite all of Bulwar. This belief, called the divine duty of Kings, was shared by the Nanšaleni harpies, which developed a parallel called the divine duty of Queens. For the Nanšaleni, their matriarch was Chosen by Surael to unite harpykind under her wing and to help the ruler of Akalšes to create peace in Surael’s garden.

Effect: True-faith tolerance: +2.

Idea 7: Legacy of Ninšara

Ninšara is the name given to the daughters of the matriarch that are born in the summer solstice and, in the same vein as Araš for Akalšes, the Nanšaleni believe that a Ninšara is destined for great deeds.

Ninšara II was born on the same day as Araš X, and both lived through the final stages of the Age of Cinders; and the rise of the Jadd. While nominally a subject of the Ayara flock, who united the harpies of the Harpy Hills, she tried to do as much as possible to remain autonomous. Eventually, during the Jaddari-Akalšesi war, she even went to help their ally and kin, defying the Ayara matriarch in the process. At the age of 67 years, she commanded the Mahdari in the battle of Traz-Buranun, where she lost a wing to Zokka Devourer-of-Darkness.

Like Araš X, she died to Andrellion, Jaddar’s firstborn son, during the last charge of the Anahallapti, fighting at horseback alongside her kin.

Effect: Monarch military power: +1.

Ambition: Nanšaleni Ambitions

Effect: Army leader shock: +1.

Hytiranyalen — Hytiranyaleni Ideas

Traditions: Hytiranyaleni Traditions

Effect: Reform progress growth: +15%; Build time: -10%.

Idea 1: The Western Harpy Migrations

Our flock was the first to leave the first Harpy Queendom, following its fracturing on the death of Firanya. We settled in Western Bahar, a region inhabited by both Dwarves and Humans. With neither intent to go further nor evict these peoples, we became adept at integrating ourselves among these communities without bloodshed.

Effect: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 2: The Odd Hunt

The Odd Hunt is our flocks proudest and most important innovation. Instead of the usual raids for mates and gold, we sought a more valuable prize; knowledge. Returning with a trove of tomes, recounts, blueprints, artifacts and wise people found along the way, we implement the learnings of our neighbors to bring advancement and prosperity to our lands and people.

Effect: Advisor cost: -10%; Possible advisors: +1.

Idea 3: Hytiranyaleni-Ayaralleni Rivalry

Our flock has long held a fierce rivalry with the Ayarallen matriarchy, frequently trading blows and clashing in the skies, constantly at war throughout our history of living in these hills. Our superiority was cemented in the battle of Šetufiraor of 490AA, where we decisively routed the Ayaralleni flock, dominating the skies of battle and driving their from our lands.

Effect: Prestige: +0.5.

Idea 4: Legacy of the Third Harpylen

The third Harpy Queendom was forged by the alliance between our flock and the Lysinyalen flock, as a bulwark against Nanšalen and their human allies of Akalšes, who in 546 AA campaigned into the eastern flocks and the Gelkar cities. Our Matriarch’s deft diplomacy and promises of land proved fruitful, and together, alongside the Gelkar, we were able to rout the Akalšesi incursion decisively in the battle of Gelkalis in 550AA, bringing an end to Nanšalen's expansion.

Effect: Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 5: All Equal Under our Wings

The lands of Hytiranya are a diverse place, inhabited by humans, elves and goblins. Our will is enforced by a deft and gentle touch, lenient policies and understanding of the differences between the peoples of our Queendom. This has led to a reputation for being a beacon of acceptance.

Effect: Number of accepted cultures: +2.

Idea 6: Shield of the Harpy Queendom

Our flock was the first to face against the Xhazobine, we were the first to weather Aakhet’s wrath, we outlasted the Castanites who came to slaughter us and were the first to bleed upon Jaher's spearpoints. Our flock is enduring and unbreakable, and no matter who we face, no matter how many times we bleed, no matter how many times we bend, we shall never break.

Effect: Morale damage received: -10%.

Idea 7: The Hunt for Science

Our borders with the Overclan allow us access to a new and evolving knowledge in our Odd Hunts, now far more diplomatic and organized in nature. Artificery; the use of Magic and Science together to create wonders is truly a treasure for the already inquisitive minds of the Hytiranyan flock, who would spread the wonders of their inventions throughout the entire Harpylen Queendom.

Effect: Technology cost: -5%.
